title: Paintings after Ancient Masters: Chrysanthemum
medium: Album leaf; ink and color on silk

image.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art, John L. Severance Fund

phase.label: Late albums, after the fall of the Ming

source.label: CMA: Chen “suffered through the violent transition from the Ming to the Qing dynasty around 1644”
Sirén: Chen “occasionally painted [flowers] besides [landscapes] or figure compositions”
Chen’s inscription: “painted in imitation of the Northern Song style”

highlight.text: Hongshou painted in imitation of the Northern Song style for Daoist friend, Cangfu.

source.author: Chen Hongshou
source.title: Inscription on Chrysanthemum
source.publisher: translated in the Cleveland Museum of Art collection record

work.text: [the models are] generally quite simple, consisting of garden stones or rocks with a few narcissi or bamboos, sometimes amplified by the knotty trunk of some old plum-tree bursting into blossom at the approach of spring.

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V

moment.text: [Bird-and-flower painting], which was cultivated as a special branch … during the [sixteenth] century, stood no longer in the same favour at the end of the [Ming] period. Such graceful and pleasant [motifs] did not correspond to the spirit of this [rather] disturbed and fateful age

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V

matters.text: As he grew chrysanthemums, Tao is associated with this flower.
This painting of chrysanthemums alludes to the poet who lived a millennium earlier during similarly fraught times.
